newsitem.title: USA: Nikkei Inc launches online U.S. consulting firm.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei Inc launches online U.S. consulting firm.

text.p: Figuring that many Americans doing business in Asia still don't understand the business climate there, Nikkei Business Publications lauched a U.S.-based online consulting company on Wednesday.
"Our goal is to help American business executives do business in Asia and be successful at it," said Douglas Kaplan, president of consulting firm Nikkei BP BizTech Inc.
The firm, launched by the giant publishing arm of Nikkei Inc of Japan, set up shop in Santa Clara, Calif. and on the World Wide Web at www.JapanBizTech.com, Kaplan said in an interview.

Using part-time services of some 20 Nikkei editors in Asia, six employees in Santa Clara will cull articles from Nikkei's 30 business and technology publications and other material from Nikkei Inc's research for posting on the Web site.
A second major service of the start-up is seminars, Kaplan said. The first one is planned for February in Silicon Valley and named "Wired into Asia." Four others will follow in 1997.
Kaplan said the firm also plans to offer various online consulting services from Nikkei Inc staff and other Asian consultants. He did not offer specifics on those services.
To generate more revenue, Nikkei BP BizTech is also trying to get advertisers on its Web site and sponsors for its seminars.

Kaplan said the Internet is starting to be a major business tool in Asia, with more business people using it than consumers. Accordingly Nikkei saw prospects of using it to network Asian and U.S. business people, especially those who already use the Internet for business purposes.
The start-up is being underwritten by Nikkei BP, whose publishing endeavors bring in about $400 million in annual revenues, he said.
